metaDescription: Six manual reel mowers compared by blade count, cutting width, height range and sharpening support, with advice on which grass types each suits.
expertTake: The Scotts 2000-20S is the pick for a flat lawn of ordinary cool-season grass where width and a wide height range matter, and the American Lawn Mower 2607-16 with seven blades is the pick for fine, short turf. Anyone with a lawn above roughly a fifth of an acre, steep slopes or tall weedy growth should skip the category and buy a rotary mower.
introParagraphs: A reel mower cuts like a pair of scissors. Blades on a spinning reel sweep grass against a fixed bar and shear it cleanly, instead of tearing it with an impact blade. The result is a tidier lawn that heals faster, with no fuel, oil or noise.

It is also a tool with real limits. Height range, blade count and adjustment decide whether it works on your turf, and reels punish neglect with stalled passes and ragged edges. The six mowers here cover the main trade-offs between width, blade count and upkeep.

products.name: Scotts 2000-20S 20-Inch 5-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.description:
The Scotts 2000-20S covers a 20 inch swath, which is the widest of the group and cuts the number of passes on a lawn by a quarter against a 16 inch machine. A five-blade ball bearing reel spins on heat-treated alloy steel blades, and a quick-snap height adjuster runs from 1 to 3 inches.

That height range is the real selling point. Most reel mowers top out below 2.5 inches, so the Scotts can handle a lawn that has been left a week too long or a cool-season grass kept a little taller in summer. The cost of width is push effort, since a 20 inch reel is harder to turn than a 14 inch one, particularly on soft ground, and the added width makes tight beds and corners more awkward. Against the LawnMaster 20 inch model it trades a lower minimum height for a higher maximum.

Ownership is mostly adjustment. Reel to bedknife contact should be a sheet of paper's worth, and the mower drifts out of adjustment after a hard season. Clear sticks before each pass, wipe the reel and lubricate pivots, and sharpen every year or two. Store it dry, since a rusty reel binds.
products.bestFor: A flat suburban lawn of ordinary grass where the widest cut and tall setting save time.
pros: 20 inch cut covers ground quickly
1 to 3 inch height range handles tall growth
Heat-treated alloy steel blades hold an edge
Ball bearing reel spins freely
cons: Wide reel takes more push effort on soft turf
Cannot cut very low for fine turf

products.name: LawnMaster LMRM2001 20-Inch 5-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.description:
The LawnMaster LMRM2001 shares the Scotts 20 inch width but gives you nine cutting positions starting at 1.3 inches. Fine height steps help when you are learning what your grass tolerates, because a quarter inch more or less changes how the mower tracks and how green the lawn stays through July.

Its 10 inch front wheels roll over minor bumps better than the small wheels of cheaper mowers, which matters because a reel can only cut what it can reach. On a lawn with dips or leaf debris, the bigger wheel pays off. It lacks the Scotts maximum height, so a lawn that has gone long will need two passes.

Expect to check the reel contact after the first few cuts because hardware settles in. Keep the wheel axles greased and rinse clippings off the reel, as damp grass cakes between blades and slows the spin.
products.bestFor: A lawn owner who wants fine control of height from a wide machine.
pros: Nine cutting positions allow fine tuning
20 inch width reduces the number of passes
10 inch front wheels roll over bumps
Scissor action leaves a clean cut
cons: 1.3 inch minimum is too high for very short turf
Wide deck is harder around beds

products.name: Great States 815-18 18-Inch 5-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.description:
The Great States 815-18 offers the widest height range among the reel mowers here, from half an inch to 2.75 inches. Few manual mowers can cut as low as half an inch, and that matters if you keep a close-clipped lawn of fine fescue or a firm hybrid turf.

An 18 inch width splits the difference between agility and coverage, and the 10 inch composite wheels roll well on level ground. The five-blade reel is a sound choice for standard residential grass, though it will not trim as fine as a seven-blade reel. Compared with the Scotts it cuts lower but gives up two inches of width.

Maintenance is classic reel work: lap or sharpen when cuts turn ragged, oil the pivots, and adjust the bedknife contact. Because the height adjuster reaches the low end, the blades can scalp bumps, so mow a smooth lawn and roll out hard dips first.
products.bestFor: A homeowner who wants a close, tidy lawn and an 18 inch cut.
pros: Cuts as low as half an inch
18 inch width balances coverage and agility
Alloy steel blades with ball bearing reel
10 inch wheels roll well on level turf
cons: Five blades are less fine than a seven-blade reel

products.name: Earthwise 1715-16EW 16-Inch 7-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.description:
The Earthwise 1715-16EW uses a seven-blade reel, which cuts finer than a five-blade by shearing more often per rotation. The maker points it at fine, dense grasses such as bent, Bermuda, Zoysia and Centipede, the turfs that suffer under a coarse cut.

Steel side frames and a ball bearing reel give a solid feel, and 10 inch wheels roll cleanly. The cost of seven blades is push effort, since more blades means more contact points and a mower you must push briskly to keep momentum. It also takes more careful setup, because seven edges must all meet the bedknife evenly.

Use it on a lawn kept short and mowed often. A reel with seven blades will struggle with tall growth, so it is a poor choice for a weekly mower of a thick cool-season lawn.
products.bestFor: Fine-bladed warm-season turf cut short and mowed often.
pros: Seven blades give a finer cut
Aimed at Bermuda, Zoysia and bentgrass lawns
Steel side frames feel sturdy
10 inch wheels roll smoothly
cons: Seven blades take more push effort
Struggles in tall or thick growth

products.name: American Lawn Mower 2607-16 16-Inch 7-Blade Reel with Sharpener
products.description:
The 2607-16 is built for fine-textured grasses such as bentgrass, Bermuda and Zoysia, with a seven-blade reel and an SK-2 hand sharpener in the box. The sharpener is the unusual part: it lets you keep the reel keen at home rather than paying for a service.

It matches the Earthwise on blade count and width, so the decision comes down to the sharpener and the brand's support. A 16 inch cut keeps it light, and the lightweight frame makes seven blades less tiring than they would be on a heavier machine.

Use the sharpener on a schedule rather than waiting for ragged cuts, since a blade that is slightly dull still cuts but starts to tear, and torn tips turn brown. Rinse clippings off after each mow and oil the pivots.
products.bestFor: A fine-turf owner who wants to sharpen the reel at home.
pros: Includes an SK-2 sharpener for home upkeep
Seven-blade reel for fine grasses
Light 16 inch body is easy to push
Made for bent, Bermuda and Zoysia
cons: Seven blades do not suit tall growth

products.name: American Lawn Mower 1304-14 14-Inch 5-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.description:
The 1304-14 is the plain-spoken member of the American Lawn Mower range: a five-blade, 14 inch reel with heat-treated alloy steel blades, 10 inch polymer wheels and a height range of 1 to 2.25 inches. It is the lightest and narrowest machine here, so it suits a small lawn with beds, trees and tight corners.

Compared with the 2607-16 it has two fewer blades and two fewer inches of width, which means a slightly coarser finish but far less push effort and more tolerance for longer grass. It does not ship with a sharpener, so budget for lapping compound or a sharpening kit later.

The usual rules apply: mow often, keep the height at the upper end for cool-season turf, and check reel contact each season. Lubricate and wipe dry before storage.
products.bestFor: A small, regularly mowed lawn where a light, simple machine is welcome.
pros: Five blades push easily and tolerate longer grass
Heat-treated alloy steel blades
14 inch body maneuvers around beds
10 inch polymer wheels roll well
cons: Narrow cut means many passes on a big lawn

buyingCriteria.explanation: Five blades suit typical residential grass mowed weekly, while seven blades suit fine, dense turf that is mowed short and often. The Earthwise 1715-16EW and the American Lawn Mower 2607-16 are seven-blade designs aimed at Bermuda and Zoysia. A seven-blade reel pushed through tall or thick grass will bog down, so match the blade count to your mowing habits, not to a spec sheet.

Reel mowers cut within a narrow range, and the numbers vary a lot. The Great States 815-18 cuts from 0.5 to 2.75 inches, the Scotts 2000-20S from 1 to 3 inches and the LawnMaster LMRM2001 from 1.3 inches upward. A cool-season lawn kept at 2.5 to 3 inches needs the Scotts range, and a close-clipped lawn needs the Great States.

A 20 inch reel like the Scotts covers ground quickly but demands more push than a 16 inch machine. Narrower reels are easier on a small yard with beds and trees. If your lawn is under a few thousand square feet, a 16 inch reel is usually less tiring over a full session than a 20 inch one.

Reels only cut what they reach, so wheel size matters. Ten inch wheels on the Scotts, LawnMaster and Earthwise ride over small bumps. Uneven ground still defeats a reel, because high spots get scalped and dips get missed. Flatten the lawn before you buy.

Reel blades dull slowly but need attention every year or two, and misalignment causes ragged cuts before dullness does. The American Lawn Mower models with an included hand sharpener let you maintain the edge at home. A mower without one needs lapping compound or a service visit.

Reel mowers suit lawns up to a few thousand square feet; past about five thousand square feet the time and effort climb quickly. They also hate long weedy growth, sticks and acorns. If your lawn gets mowed twice a month rather than weekly, a reel will frustrate you.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cut quality design
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed blade count and the reel design against the grass types makers name. Seven-blade reels earned credit for fine turf and five-blade reels for general lawns.

howWeEvaluated.title: Height range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated minimum and maximum heights, since this decides which grasses a mower can serve. The Great States at 0.5 to 2.75 inches and the Scotts at 1 to 3 inches are the widest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Effort and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered width, wheel size and blade count together as a measure of push effort. A 16 inch five-blade is the easiest, and a 20 inch the most tiring.

howWeEvaluated.title: Upkeep support
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted included sharpeners and ball bearing reels as practical advantages. The American models with sharpeners score best.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit for lawn size
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched cutting widths to realistic yard sizes, favouring narrower machines for small lawns with beds and wider ones for open turf.

cards.label: Five blades
cards.text: The Scotts, LawnMaster, Great States and American 1304-14 use five blades. They push easier, tolerate longer grass and suit most lawns mowed weekly.

cards.label: Seven blades
cards.text: The Earthwise and American 2607-16 use seven blades for a finer cut on dense warm-season grass. They require brisk pushing and shorter grass.

howToChoose.note: Five blades for ordinary lawns; seven for fine turf you mow often.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Flat Suburban Lawn Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a mower with a height range that matches your grass, a width you can push for the whole lawn, and wheels large enough to ride small bumps. Flat ground is a must.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Scotts 2000-20S fits an ordinary grass lawn and the Great States 815-18 fits one kept short. Both are five-blade, ball bearing machines.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you keep fine turf short and want a seven-blade reel plus a sharpener, as on the American 2607-16. Also spend more for the Scotts if you need the 3 inch height.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if your lawn is small and regularly mowed. The American 1304-14 is light, simple and costs least. Add a sharpening kit later and it will serve for years.

maintenance.why: The reel should just touch the bedknife and cut a sheet of paper. Misalignment causes ragged cuts before dullness does.
Dull blades tear the tips of grass and turn them brown. A hand sharpener or lapping compound restores the edge.
A twig between reel and bedknife stalls the mower and nicks the blade.
Dry pivots stiffen the height adjuster and raise push effort.
Rust on the reel binds the blades. Wipe clippings off and store indoors.

faq.q: Are reel mowers good for any lawn?
faq.a: They suit flat lawns of a few thousand square feet that are mowed weekly. They struggle with tall weeds, sticks and uneven ground. A rotary mower is a better choice for rough or large lawns.

faq.q: How many blades do I need?
faq.a: Five blades suit most residential grass, and seven suit fine, dense warm-season grass kept short. More blades push harder and cut best at brisk walking speed.

faq.q: How often do reel mowers need sharpening?
faq.a: Every one to two years for normal use, or when the cut looks torn. Adjusting the reel contact often fixes a ragged cut before sharpening is needed.

faq.q: Can I cut tall grass with a reel mower?
faq.a: Only to the upper height setting, about 2.75 to 3 inches on the models here. Cut tall grass in stages, raising the height first and lowering it over several mows.

faq.q: Do reel mowers really damage grass less?
faq.a: The scissor cut leaves cleaner tips than a rotary blade and the lawn tends to look better. The benefit is modest if the rotary blade is sharp.

faq.q: Why does my reel mower leave uncut strips?
faq.a: Usually the blades are out of adjustment or dull, or the grass is too tall for the height setting. Check contact, sharpen the blades and mow more often.
